subject: social_science

concepts.title: The Idea of a Supreme God
concepts.section: The Idea of a Supreme God
concepts.definition: The conceptual framework stating that devotion to a single divine entity enables individuals to overcome cosmic cycles of rebirth and social inequality.
concepts.key_idea: Devotional approach offered personal liberation from societal hierarchies and birth cycles.
question_patterns: what is the concept of a supreme god in early devotional traditions
explain how the idea of devotion offered an alternative to caste inequality
describe the belief regarding rebirth and salvation in early bhakti
why did people turn toward the idea of a single supreme deity
how did puranic texts promote the concept of divine grace for all

solution_steps.explain: Growth of towns and empires brought diverse groups together, while learned texts promoted birth-based social privileges and rebirth cycles.
Bhakti proposed that approaching a Supreme God with love allows any person to transcend social barriers and achieve spiritual deliverance.

concepts.title: Nayanars and Alvars of South India
concepts.section: Bhakti in South India - Nayanars and Alvars
concepts.definition: Tamil saint-poets dedicated to Shiva or Vishnu who travelled singing compositions, drawing inspiration from Sangam poetry and inclusion across all castes.
concepts.key_idea: South Indian saint-poets democratized devotion through vernacular music and poetry.
question_patterns: who were the nayanars and alvars in southern india
compare the devotion of nayanars with that of alvars
describe the role of tevaram and divya prabandham in Tamil bhakti
how did temple construction by kings strengthen the bhakti movement
explain the inclusion of lower castes among south indian saint poets

solution_steps.explain: Nayanars were 63 saints devoted to Shiva; Alvars were 12 saints devoted to Vishnu, both arising from varied caste backgrounds.

solution_steps.action: Examine their literary and cultural legacy
solution_steps.explain: Their musical poetry was compiled in sacred collections like Tevaram, Tiruvacakam, and Divya Prabandham, supported later by Chola and Pandya royal temples.

concepts.title: Philosophical Foundations: Advaita and Vishishtadvaita
concepts.definition: Philosophical doctrines formulated by Shankara and Ramanuja explaining the relationship between the individual soul and the supreme reality.
concepts.key_idea: Shankara taught non-dualism while Ramanuja emphasized devotion to attain union with God.
question_patterns: what is the philosophical doctrine of advaita propounded by shankara
explain ramanuja idea of vishishtadvaita and qualified oneness
differentiate between the teachings of shankara and ramanuja
describe how ramanuja philosophy influenced northern bhakti movement
identify the main tenets regarding brahman and illusion in advaita

solution_steps.explain: Advaita advocates the non-duality of the individual soul and Brahman, viewing the material world as an illusion (maya).
Vishishtadvaita posits that the soul remains distinct even when united with Vishnu, emphasizing intense devotion for salvation.

concepts.title: Virashaivism and Basavanna
concepts.definition: A twelfth-century socio-religious movement in Karnataka led by Basavanna advocating equality, rejecting caste and ritualism through vachanas.
concepts.key_idea: Virashaivism challenged ritualistic orthodoxy and Brahmanical social privileges.
question_patterns: what were the primary teachings of basavanna virashaiva movement
explain how virashaivas viewed caste distinctions and rituals
describe the main themes expressed in basavanna vachanas
why did virashaivism oppose temple worship and idol worship
identify the key leaders associated with the virashaiva movement

solution_steps.explain: Initiated in mid-12th century Karnataka by Basavanna alongside Allama Prabhu and Akkamahadevi.
Argued for human equality, opposed caste and gender discrimination, and rejected temple rituals and idol worship through poetry (vachanas).

concepts.title: Bhakti Tradition in Maharashtra
concepts.definition: A regional devotional tradition centered around Vitthala in Pandharpur, emphasizing worldly living, family life, and empathy for others.
concepts.key_idea: Marathi saint-poets rejected worldly renunciation in favor of family life and social compassion.
question_patterns: who were the prominent saint poets of the maharashtra bhakti movement
explain the significance of the vitthala temple at pandharpur
describe the humanist outlook of Marathi saints like tukaram
how did maharashtra saints re-define true devotion and saintliness
identify the social background of chokhamela family in maharashtra bhakti

solution_steps.explain: Dnyaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, Tukaram, Sakhubai, and Chokhamela's family composed Marathi songs (abhangs).
Centered on Vitthala at Pandharpur, rejected ascetism, lived with families while serving others, defining devotion as sharing pain.

concepts.title: Nathpanthis, Siddhas, and Yogis
concepts.definition: Ascetic groups advocating world renunciation, body-mind mastery through yogic practices, and logical critique of orthodox religion.
concepts.key_idea: Yogic meditation and physical discipline were used to realize formless ultimate reality.
question_patterns: what were the methods adopted by nathpanthis siddhas and yogis for salvation
describe the criticism of conventional religion by yogic groups
explain the practices used by nathpanthis to discipline body and mind
why did renunciatory groups gain popularity among lower caste groups
identify the path to ultimate reality according to siddhacharas

solution_steps.explain: Advocated renunciation of the world and meditation on formless ultimate reality using logical arguments against formal rituals.
Employed yogasanas, breathing exercises, and intense mental training, becoming especially popular among lower castes.

concepts.title: Sufism and Islamic Mysticism
concepts.definition: Mystical branch of Islam focusing on intense personal devotion to God, compassion, spiritual discipline under a pir, and hospice culture.
concepts.key_idea: Sufis emphasized divine love, devotional music, and universal humanitarian compassion.
question_patterns: what are the central beliefs and practices of sufi mystics
explain the role of khanqahs and dargahs in sufi culture
describe the contribution of the chishti silsila in India
how did Sufi orders integrate practices like zikr and sama
identify major sufi masters associated with the Delhi Sultanate period

solution_steps.explain: Rejected orthodox ritualism, seeking direct union with God through love, compassion, zikr (chanting), and sama (music).
Operated through spiritual lineages (silsilas) centered around hospices (khanqahs) and tombs (dargahs), notably the Chishti order.

concepts.title: Late Medieval North Indian Bhakti Surge
concepts.section: New Religious Developments in North India
concepts.definition: Fourteenth-to-sixteenth century devotional resurgence featuring both saguna and nirguna poets composing in regional vernaculars.
concepts.key_idea: Bhakti saints used accessible regional languages to express diverse forms of personal devotion.
question_patterns: how did north indian bhakti movement evolve after the thirteenth century
describe the literary contributions of tulsidas and surdas
explain mirabai devotion to krishna and her defiance of royal norms
what was shankardeva contribution to assamese bhakti culture
why did vernacular compositions become popular among common masses

solution_steps.explain: Included Nirguna proponents (Kabir, Nanak) and Saguna devotees like Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas), Surdas (Sursagara), Mirabai, and Shankardeva.
Songs were composed in regional languages (Awadhi, Braj, Assamese) and transmitted orally by marginalized groups and women.

concepts.title: Kabir's Devotional Philosophy
concepts.definition: A radical fifteenth-century saint from Varanasi who rejected formal rituals, priestcraft, and social divisions through sharp vernacular verses.
concepts.key_idea: Kabir advocated formless supreme devotion while rejecting external rituals of Hinduism and Islam.
question_patterns: what were the major teachings of Kabir against ritualism
describe the literary sources used to reconstruct Kabir ideas
explain Kabir concept of formless supreme god
how did Kabir express his criticism of priestly authority
identify where Kabir compositions are compiled and preserved

solution_steps.explain: Ridiculed external rituals, priestly dominance, and caste system of both Brahmanical Hinduism and Islam, advocating devotion to a formless God.
Compositions expressed in spoken Hindi (sakhis and pads), preserved in Guru Granth Sahib, Panch Vani, and Bijak.

concepts.title: Teachings and Legacy of Baba Guru Nanak
concepts.section: A Closer Look: Baba Guru Nanak
concepts.definition: Fifteenth-century spiritual leader who established monotheistic worship, communal dining, and active social responsibility leading to the Khalsa identity.
concepts.key_idea: Guru Nanak emphasized one God, active householder life, equality, and social welfare.
question_patterns: what were the main teachings of Baba Guru Nanak regarding God and social life
explain the significance of dharamsal langar and gurmukhi
describe the compilation process of the Guru Granth Sahib
how did the Sikh community develop into a political entity by seventeenth century
what did Guru Nanak mean by nam dan and ishnan

solution_steps.explain: Emphasized worship of one God, rejected caste/gender inequalities, established common kitchen (langar) and worship hall (dharamsal/gurdwara).
Guru Angad introduced Gurmukhi; Guru Arjan compiled Guru Granth Sahib (1604); Guru Gobind Singh established the Khalsa Panth (1699).

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain how the Virashaiva movement challenged traditional social and religious practices.

solution_template.explain: Initiated in 12th century Karnataka by Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, and Akkamahadevi.
They rejected Brahmanical ideas on caste, advocated equal treatment of women, and opposed all forms of temple ritual and idol worship.

worked_examples.source_ref: Textbook comparison of Sufi and Bhakti traditions
worked_examples.question_pattern: Describe the key similarities between Sufi mystics and Bhakti saint-poets.

solution_template.explain: Both groups prioritized personal love and devotion to God over ritualistic codes of conduct.
Both rejected religious bigotry, expressed ideas in vernacular poetry, and emphasized universal brotherhood and compassion.
